question.text: Nucleus a having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></math> and equal number of protons and neutrons has <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math> binding energy per nucleon. Another nucleus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> has total <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>26</mn></math> nucleons and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math> binding energy per nucleons. The difference of binding energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>MeV</mi></math>.

solution.text:
In A, Z=17 and have equal numbers of protons and neutrons i.e. nucleons=2×17=34

So, for A, 

Total binding energy BEA=1.2×34=40.8 MeV

Another nucleus B mass number =26

So, total binding energy of  B is BEB=1.8×26 MeV=46.8 MeV

Difference of BE=BEB-BEA=6 MeV
